rows.title: American Sign Language I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will utilize American Sign Language to express and receive information about a variety of topics at a beginner level.
Students will demonstrate accuracy and proficiency in the use of learned structures and vocabulary.
Students will differentiate the unique cultural aspects of American Deaf culture from the unique cultural aspects of other cultures.
objectives: Integrate American Sign Language (ASL) vocabulary, grammar and culture to introduce self and others, exchange personal information, talk and ask about surroundings (spatial agreement), telling and asking where people live (signer's perspective), converse about family, express opinions, talk about past, present and future activities.
Identify and apply the phonology of ASL to each sign by using the five parameters (handshape, palm orientation, location, movement, and non-manual behaviors) accurately and appropriately.
Identify and analyze similarities and differences in the American Deaf and hearing cultures.
Comprehend and generate short story narratives and conversations utilizing all elements of ASL grammar and phonology accurately.
Utilize American Sign Language grammar correctly to communicate a variety of activities and real world experiences.

rows.title: Observation and Assessment for Early Learning and Development (DS3)
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Complete systematic observations and assessments of children’s development and learning using a variety of data collection methods to inform classroom teaching, environment design, interactions, and curriculum.
Evaluate the characteristics, strengths, limitations, and applications of contemporary observation and assessment tools.
Describe the ethical and professional responsibilities for educators in observing and assessing young children’s development and learning.
objectives: Discuss the role of partnerships with families and other professionals in utilizing interpretations of observational and assessment data.
Describe legal and ethical responsibilities in relation to observation, assessment, documentation, and recordkeeping.
Demonstrate how observation and assessment are used to plan for and adjust learning experiences.
Discuss logistical challenges, biases, and preconceptions about observing and assessing children.
Use standardized observation and assessment tools to evaluate quality in environments, interactions, and curriculum.
Apply knowledge of development and other influencing factors to interpret observations and assessments.
Differentiate between various observation and assessment tools according to their purpose and validity.
Demonstrate basic formative and summative assessment techniques.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate successful completion of all Physical Ability Test events without assistance with a passing score of 9 minutes and 34 seconds or less.
objectives: Demonstrate the physical skills, strength, endurance, and coordination required to complete all Biddle Firefighter Physical Ability Test tasks safely and within the validated time standard.
Apply proper techniques for each manipulative task to ensure safe, efficient, and effective performance under test and field conditions.
Evaluate their current level of physical preparedness through structured practice, feedback, and timed assessments.
Develop an individualized exercise and conditioning program designed to enhance performance, address areas of improvement, and reduce injury risk.
Incorporate sound nutrition and recovery strategies into a personal wellness plan that supports training, testing, and long-term occupational fitness.

rows.title: Principles of Retailing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: develop the communication, information and reasoning skills necessary in the retail work environment to increase productivity and enhance career opportunities.
create hypotheses, compare and contrast possible problem solutions, analyze possible outcomes and recommend action plans in the ratail management business environment.

rows.title: Introduction to Pharmacy Technology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the duties and roles of the pharmacy technician in various practice settings.
Identify the skills needed to successfully complete the Pharmacy Technology program at SAC.
Summarize the license and certification process for pharmacy technicians.
Differentiate drugs classified as OTC, Rx, (federal legend) C1, C2, C3, C4, C5.
Identify the steps involved in new drug development.
Discuss the characteristics of common drug dosage forms.
Memorize the 100 common trade-generic equivalents and indications.
Interpret prescriptions, memorize prescription sig codes, and prepare prescription labels.
objectives: Memorize the top 100 common trade-generic medication names.
Demonstrate an understanding of the characteristics of common dosage forms.
Explain all the steps involved in new drug development.
Understand the system of drug classification.
Demonstrate the ability to read prescriptions and prepare prescription labels.
Explain in depth which skills are needed to successfully complete the Pharmacy Technology program.
Analyze and discuss the duties and roles of the pharmacy technician in various practice settings.

rows.title: Introduction to Communicative Disorders and Treatment
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic terminology related to the field of communicative disorders.
Demonstrate knowledge of the basic principles of evaluating and treating individuals with communication disorders.
objectives: Identify and describe the anatomy and physiology of the speech and voice mechanism.
Describe the roles, responsibilities, and work settings of speech-language pathologists.
Define and explain the basic terminology related to human communication disorders.
Identify and classify various types of communication disorders.
Discuss the basic principles of human speech, language, and hearing development across the life span.
Discuss professional aspects of speech-language pathology including professional ethics, legal guidelines, certification, and licensure requirements.
Discuss the impact of communication disorders on peoples' lives.
Describe and discuss the basic principles of assessment and remediation of various types of communication disorders.
